A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEEM study and include appendices A-E. Text and visual inspection support matching the methods, equations, experiments, tables and examples despite reflow and localized layout defects.

before.justification: v1 reports original DEEM benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative generation examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds an empirical comparison of RobustVQA question formats in Table 5.

M1.justification: The architecture, mask-aware extractor, consistency semantic regularization, three-stage training objectives and inference procedure remain unchanged. The added question-format experiment does not modify DEEM.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including RobustVQA, POPE, VQA, captioning, regional understanding and image generation. New Table 5 varies prompts for existing RobustVQA object-recognition tasks without adding data populations or domains.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark tables retain their comparator sets. New Table 5 examines the already evaluated MM-Interleaved model; it introduces no additional comparison method against DEEM.

E3.justification: v2 Table 5 adds controlled tests of two multiple-choice option orders against yes/no prompts. Yes/no evaluation was already specified in v1 Appendix D.1 and Figure 8, so this is an added protocol comparison, not evidence that the retained benchmark evaluations changed.

E4.justification: New Table 5 adds a question-format and option-order sensitivity analysis identifying MM-Interleaved's first-option preference. Existing regularization, latency, resolution, loss-weight and module-freezing ablations, plus qualitative case studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Table 5 adds point accuracies; its description of greater stability does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds MM-Interleaved multiple-choice accuracies of 44.88/58.88/46.86 with the false label first and 84.60/90.16/82.92 with ground truth first on RobustVQA-A/R/V. Its yes/no scores and the retained benchmark and ablation tables are unchanged. Figure 6 recombines previously reported stage-specific results rather than establishing new performance gains.

T1.justification: The likelihood formulation, losses in Equations (1)-(5), and training-stage objectives are unchanged. Neither version adds separate theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: RobustVQA, diffusion-based semantic regularization, improved robustness and hallucination handling with fewer resources, and multimodal downstream capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that multiple-choice evaluation is vulnerable to option-order bias and uses this to justify yes/no questions. Appendix A's limitations concerning robustness forgetting after fine-tuning and the cost of updating larger encoders remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a repository pointer and states that code and benchmark are available; v1 only promises release in Appendix C. That future-release wording persists in v2, so the PDFs do not establish release completeness. Existing implementation details and training recipes are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including comparisons with MM-Interleaved and DreamLLM. The bibliography retains the same 70 references.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited spacing, terminology and explanatory edits, including spacing around DEEM and the added format-selection rationale. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, adjusts figure and table placement, and resizes Figure 11 so its clipped caption becomes readable. Figure 6 changes radial scaling and replaces separate DEEM and DEEM-SFT curves with one DEEM curve combining pretraining RobustVQA scores and fine-tuned POPE scores.

improvement.justification: Table 5 supplies useful empirical support for the existing yes/no evaluation choice, while the access pointer and repaired Figure 11 improve usability. These are limited gains. Figure 6 becomes less transparent by pooling results from different training stages, but unchanged Table 1 and Appendix A still disclose the stage-specific results and robustness tradeoff, limiting that drawback.
